clue.text: Firm stand taken about many an article

indicators.note: the firm-and-stand pair is wrapped around the letter for many, which sits between them

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a stand on an issue is a position
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many

explanation.surface: A company takes a public stance on a great many news items.
explanation.definitionFit: A written piece such as a school essay is a composition, and an article is such a piece of writing.

clue.text: Copper leading one-time coppers? The sauce!

parts.note: CU is the chemical symbol for copper
a leading performer is the star
d stood for the old pre-decimal British pennies, copper coins

explanation.surface: A senior policeman heads a squad of retired officers, prompting an indignant cry about their cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coppers' suggests police, but here it means copper coins: d was the abbreviation for an old British penny before 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: Custard is a sweet yellow pouring sauce served over puddings.

clue.text: No subordinate Oriental state

parts.note: what is not subordinate is the main or chief one
E stands for East, the Orient

explanation.surface: A statement that someone is no underling of an Eastern master.
explanation.definitionFit: Maine is a US state in New England.

clue.text: Order fiddle in case-and bow

parts.note: the OBE is the Order of the British Empire

indicators.note: to fiddle with something is to tamper and rearrange it, so these letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Instructions to play the fiddle while it is still in its case, and to bow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddle' and 'bow' both suggest a violin, but 'fiddle' is the anagram signal and 'bow' is a deferential bend.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeisance is a gesture of respect such as a bow or curtsy.

clue.text: Feature some quite memorable work

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are used, a run across them

explanation.surface: A magazine feature about a fairly memorable piece of work.
explanation.definitionFit: A news item is a single feature or piece in a paper or programme.

clue.text: Popular nurse. She swears!

parts.note: IN means popular or fashionable
a senior nurse is called a sister in Britain

explanation.surface: A well-liked nurse who has a habit of swearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swears' suggests bad language, but here it means affirms firmly; a British sister is a senior ward nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: One who swears something is so is one who insists on it, a person who keeps asserting.

clue.text: The girl's comeuppance would make one lament

indicators.note: read as come-up, the letters rise, so in a down clue they are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
to lament is to moan

explanation.surface: A girl gets her just deserts, which would make anyone mourn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comeuppance' looks like punishment, but split as 'come up' it turns I MOAN backwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi is a female first name, so a girl.

clue.text: A reformer's last word with the German

parts.note: amen is the word said at the end of a prayer
DER is a German word for the

explanation.surface: A campaigner for change has the final say alongside a German colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: One who amends things is one who corrects or improves them, as a reformer does.

clue.text: Help to raise large family getting much criticism

indicators.note: raising lifts the letters, so in this down entry the word for help is read upwards

parts.note: aid means help
a tribe is a large family group or clan

explanation.surface: Assistance in bringing up a big family attracts a lot of disapproval.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter, sustained verbal attack, a lot of criticism at once.

clue.text: Yellow invertebrate

definitions.meaning: an invertebrate is a creature without a backbone

explanation.definitionFit: Lacking a backbone literally describes an invertebrate, and figuratively describes a cowardly, weak-willed person.

clue.text: Admitting few in accord will appear sheepish

annotationWithheld.why: Admitting few in accord will appear sheepish (5): OVINE is O(VI)NE, ONE (accord) around VI, but 'few' cannot give VI; likely an OCR misread (perhaps 'six') and no scan or search confirms the printed word.
annotationWithheld.clue: Admitting few in accord will appear sheepish

clue.text: As ever, awfully hostile

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done badly, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A remark that someone is, as always, terribly unfriendly.
explanation.definitionFit: Being averse to something means being opposed or antagonistic to it.

clue.text: First to get involved in dope, top journalist was helpful

parts.note: a dope is a fool, an ass
1ST, written IST, is the abbreviation for first
ED is the editor, the senior journalist

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor first got mixed up in drugs, yet proved useful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dope' suggests drugs but means a fool; 'First' is written as the abbreviation 1st, with the digit read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: To have assisted is to have helped out or aided someone.

clue.text: Expected retired woman to be chaperone

parts.note: something due is expected

indicators.note: a retired thing has gone back, so the woman's name is read backwards

parts.note: Ann is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A pensioner is expected to accompany a young lady as her escort.
explanation.definitionFit: A duenna is an older woman who acts as a governess and escort for a young girl, especially in Spain.

clue.text: Assembly point-nicer to change this

parts.note: E is East, a point of the compass

indicators.note: change means alter, so the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A meeting point would be nicer if someone altered it.
explanation.definitionFit: The erection of a structure is its assembly or building.

clue.text: Wise man making "mole" rich

indicators.note: making something of these letters means reworking them into a new order

explanation.surface: A sage turns a small burrowing animal into a wealthy one.
explanation.definitionFit: Melchior is traditionally one of the three Magi who visited the infant Jesus.

clue.text: An officer of the law studies the register

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a table is a list or register of figures

explanation.surface: A policeman looks over the official roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A constable is a police officer of the lowest rank.

clue.text: Hector is to join the Left

parts.note: BE is the verb of which is is a form
the Labour Party is the main left-wing party in Britain

explanation.surface: Hector is to become a member of the left-wing party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hector' looks like a man's name, but it is the verb meaning bully; Labour is Britain's main party of the left.
explanation.definitionFit: To hector someone is to harangue them, and to belabour is likewise to attack or berate verbally.

clue.text: Quietly fell back or went ahead

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction to play quietly
to recede is to fall back or withdraw

explanation.surface: Someone either silently retreated or pressed forward.
explanation.definitionFit: To have preceded something is to have come before it, to have gone in front.

clue.text: Associate holding up inevitable survey

indicators.note: the word for associate holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: a pal is a friend or associate

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: something sure is certain, inevitable

explanation.surface: A colleague delays an unavoidable inspection.
explanation.definitionFit: A perusal is a reading or examination of something, a survey of it.

clue.text: Aim for 25

definitions.meaning: to aim to do something is to plan to do it
the answer to 25 down, a word meaning to have in mind

explanation.walkthrough: '25' points to the answer at 25 down, which as a verb means to have in mind.
explanation.definitionFit: To intend is to aim or plan, and also to mean something, as with meaning no harm.

clue.text: Hates taking notes before exams

parts.note: D and E are musical notes
exams are tests

explanation.surface: Someone loathes having to take notes before sitting exams.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest is to hate or loathe intensely.

clue.text: A liar not perhaps capable of reasoning

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Doubting whether a liar might be able to think logically.
explanation.definitionFit: A rational being is one able to think logically and use reason.

clue.text: Circles around people, making signs

indicators.note: the two circles go around the people, one on each side

parts.note: O is a circle in shape, so two of them give OS
men are people

explanation.surface: Groups gather around folk who are gesturing.
explanation.definitionFit: Omens are portents, signs of what is to come.

clue.text: The way a good man encompasses natural growth

indicators.note: to encompass is to surround, so the good man goes around the growth

parts.note: ST, saint, is a good man
a tree is a natural growth

explanation.surface: The path of righteousness includes developing naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: A street is a road, a way through a town.

clue.text: Plug in the previous day, duck!

indicators.note: the plug is placed in the middle of the previous day

parts.note: the eve is the day before an event
to plug a product is to advertise it, and an AD is an advertisement

explanation.surface: Someone warns to get down while plugging in something the day before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plug' suggests an electrical socket, but means a promotional mention, an ad.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck a question is to evade or dodge it.

clue.text: Low average

definitions.meaning: the average of figures is their arithmetic middle

explanation.definitionFit: A mean act is low and shabby, and the mean of a set of numbers is its average.

clue.text: A number achieve success

definitions.meaning: twenty, as in threescore years and ten
to succeed, as in scoring a goal or a hit

explanation.definitionFit: A score is the number twenty, and to score is to succeed, for example in winning points or a conquest.

clue.text: Lays down the law on certain wild animals

parts.note: over means on or above
bears are a kind of wild animal

explanation.surface: Someone dictates rules about particular beasts of the forest.
explanation.definitionFit: To overbear is to dominate or domineer, imposing one's will on others.

clue.text: Sense grants may be made to convert the odd property

indicators.note: the letters are forced to change into another form, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A suggestion that funding awards could be used to convert an unusual building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'property' suggests real estate, but here it is a quality; 'odd' is that quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Strangeness is the quality of being odd or unusual.
